problem: Embodied AI spans many separate benchmarks (navigation, rearrangement, embodied vision-and-language) with different tasks, metrics and datasets, and there is no single view of what works across them or where the field is heading.
motivation: The CVPR Embodied AI Workshop ran 13 challenges over 2020-2022. Comparing the winning entries gives a chance to find shared design patterns (large-scale training, pre-training, modular vs end-to-end, augmentation) and to point out open problems and future directions.
key_idea: Survey the 13 CVPR Embodied AI Workshop challenges (setups, metrics, state-of-the-art), extract common approaches among the winning entries, and lay out future research directions.
insight: Winning entries across challenges share four trends: large-scale training (ProcTHOR-10K, HM3D, Habitat-Web), pre-trained visual encoders (EmbCLIP), modular pipelines, and visual/dynamics augmentation. Table 1 shows end-to-end and modular methods are comparable on short-horizon tasks (ObjectNav, audio-visual navigation), but modular methods win by a large margin on long-horizon tasks (RxR-Habitat 45.82 vs 13.93 SR, rearrangement 28.94 vs 0.5), likely because exploration complexity grows with horizon length when training end-to-end with RL alone. Agents overfit heavily to training scenes (near 100% seen vs 30-50% unseen success), which motivates scaling up environments and procedural generation.
method: Challenge review: describes each of the 13 challenges (PointNav, Interactive/Social Nav, ObjectNav, MultiON, RVSU Semantic SLAM, Audio-Visual Nav, Scene Change Detection, AI2-THOR Rearrangement, TDW-Transport, RxR-Habitat, ALFRED, TEACh, etc.) with tasks, observation/action spaces, datasets, metrics, and winning results.
Common-approach analysis: compares winning entries along large-scale training, visual pre-training (EmbCLIP), end-to-end vs modular, and visual/dynamics augmentation.
End-to-end vs modular comparison (Table 1): tabulates the best end-to-end and best modular entry per 2022 challenge with success and rank.
Future directions: discusses pre-training, world models and inverse graphics, simulation/dataset advances, sim2real, procedural generation, generalist agents, multi-agent and human interaction.

setting.backbone: n/a (survey of challenge entries, e.g. ProcTHOR CLIP-ResNet50 + GRU, Habitat-Web, modular mapping and planning systems)
setting.observation: varies per challenge (egocentric RGB/RGB-D, GPS+compass, binaural audio, language)
setting.action_space: varies (discrete Move Forward 0.25 m / Rotate 30°, continuous twist commands, high-level interactive actions)
setting.simulator: Habitat, iGibson, AI2-THOR/RoboTHOR, SoundSpaces, ThreeDWorld, BenchBot/Isaac Sim

numbers_note: Survey paper without its own method; it reports challenge-winner results from other teams, which are not reproduced as the paper's own numbers.
results: The paper reports a striking jump in Habitat PointNav-v2 (SPL 0.21 in 2020 to 0.74 in 2021) and ProcTHOR state-of-the-art on RoboTHOR (SPL 0.2884, SR 65%) and Habitat 2022 ObjectNav (SPL 0.32, SR 54%). Habitat-Web RL fine-tuning reaches 60% SR on Habitat 2022 ObjectNav. Modular methods beat end-to-end ones by a wide margin on long-horizon tasks (Table 1).
limitations: Descriptive retrospective limited to challenges at one workshop (CVPR 2020-2022); no new experiments or controlled comparisons.
Winner comparisons are confounded by differing compute, data and simulators, and some cited results are unpublished.
